summary.headline: Sundram Fasteners Q1 FY27 consolidated turnover rose 20% to INR1,618 crores from INR1,367 crores; standalone profit up ~10% to INR150 crores.
summary.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as a very good start, with consolidated turnover up 20% YoY to INR1,618 crores and growth across OE, aftermarket and exports. Standalone profit rose from INR138 crores to INR150 crores, which management attributed to tighter control of fixed costs. Input cost inflation linked to the West Asia conflict was a pressure, with direct materials passed through to domestic OEMs and indirect/energy costs under negotiation. Management guided to margin expansion in Q2 once indirect cost recoveries are accounted for, and said the 20% run rate should hold through the festive period.

segments.name: Standalone exports
segments.commentary: Standalone exports grew upwards of 20% YoY in dollar terms; North American passenger car ICE volumes recovered and Class 8 truck primary orders were 20-25% above last year, with backlogs at a 38-month high as of June.

segments.name: Domestic auto (M&HCV, PV, tractor)
segments.commentary: Management said M&HCV industry grew ~20% in Q1 and SFL growth almost matched it; PV industry grew ~23% with SFL matching; tractors grew ~14-15%, roughly in line. Two-wheeler/three-wheeler (5-6% of mix) is an under-indexed area.

segments.name: Non-auto: wind energy, aerospace
segments.commentary: Wind energy fasteners moved from INR25 crores to INR30 crores per month after an expansion; a further ~INR100 crores capex is planned to lift annualised run rate from INR350 crores to INR500 crores. Aerospace revenue was ~INR50 crores, targeted at INR100 crores+ this year and INR500 crores in 2-3 years.

segments.name: EV (General Motors, Stellantis)
segments.commentary: EV revenue from General Motors was under INR50 crores in FY26 and is planned at INR200-250 crores in FY27 (combined with Stellantis), on track per Q1. EV overall is 4-5% of revenue.

segments.name: Subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Sundram Fasteners China expected to grow close to 20% this year; UK subsidiary tracking European truck market; TVS Upasana (two-wheeler) growing well. Management expects all subsidiaries to grow broadly in line with standalone.

guidance_outlook: Q2 and Q3 export outlook described as strong; run rate of ~20% growth expected to continue given festivals and customer schedules.
EBITDA margin expected to rise from 16.1% toward ~16.5% and expand further in Q2 as indirect material negotiations are accounted.
Retains FY27 growth assumptions of CV 8%, PV 10%, tractor 7% (vs industry CV 4%, tractor flat to 2%) but flagged high H2 FY26 base; may recalibrate in a quarter or so.
Capex this year quoted at around INR400 crores, of which ~30% is replacement and the balance growth; earlier guidance was ~INR250 crores.
Hyundai and Kia fasteners entry targeted at INR100 crores+ over 2-3 years.
capex_capacity: Wind energy fasteners: further expansion of close to INR100 crores to lift annualised capacity from INR350 crores to INR500 crores.
Project lead times run about 12-18 months; management is looking at asset purchases to shorten them, but said no advanced inorganic deal is in pipeline.
Imported machinery is being monitored case by case due to the West Asia crisis to protect commissioning timelines.
Digital: IoT deployed across all plants, delivering 5-10% productivity gain with 0.2-0.5% margin benefit; AS/RS systems being added.
Powder metallurgy capacity being expanded to serve passenger car, shock absorber and consumer durable customers.
demand_pricing: Direct raw materials (steel) are passed through to OEMs under contract; indirect/energy costs (e.g., LPG) are being negotiated, with recovery expected to lift Q2 margins.
Aftermarket pricing is adjusted to reflect cost inflation; exports are partly protected by rupee depreciation.
Europe is sub-20% of exports; Garrett Motion business won in two divisions (turbocharger machined parts) and ZF work at Sri City; more RFQs pending.
Standard fastener share with each OEM is 30-40% (50-60% share of business where supplied); specials are single-sourced.
New OEM entries via BIS/QCO norms at Hyundai and Kia; Cummins fasteners business growing; new pipeline of over INR1,000 crores with an equal amount under discussion.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 20% growth came from raw material inflation, and what was volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume grew about 13% in tonnage; raw material inflation contributed roughly INR20-25 crores to the top line.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company losing domestic market share given industry growth of 20%+ vs SFL's 16% domestic growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth matched industry in M&HCV (~20%), PV (~23%) and tractors (~14-15%); the gap is mainly 2W/3W, which is only 5-6% of revenue and where SFL is not present.

qa_highlights.question: What are the GM and Stellantis EV revenue expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: GM EV revenue was under INR50 crores in FY26 and is planned at INR200-250 crores this year, including Stellantis; management will take it one year at a time, with INR750 crores cited as a past peak projection.

qa_highlights.question: Where will the cash conversion cycle stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it should stay around current levels, around 140-150 days, as higher export share lengthens the operating cycle; DSO has come down and the spike is mainly inventory timing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan for this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited around INR400 crores, about 30% for replacement and the rest growth, and said investment will continue as an industry norm.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 20% growth pace hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the current run rate to hold, supported by festivals and indicative customer schedules.

risks_watch: Indirect material and energy cost inflation (West Asia conflict) still under negotiation; margin recovery depends on Q2 settlements.
Working capital: cash conversion cycle elevated at 150+ days; inventory days spiked and need to normalise toward 140-150 days.
High H2 FY26 base may compress percentage growth; management may recalibrate FY27 segment growth rates in a quarter or so.
Imported machinery delays from the West Asia crisis could affect capex commissioning.
Defence business is at an early startup stage with long validation cycles; EV revenue ramp depends on GM and Stellantis schedules.

There is a press release about INR400 crores. Any year, if you see last three years balance sheet, it is roughly around those levels.
Maybe we will finish closer to 16.5.
Maybe a quarter or so later, maybe we can calibrate.

summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and the balance sheet: management called Q1 a very good start, said liquidity is not a concern, and expects the 20% run rate to hold. Cautious on input costs and H2 base effects, with indirect-cost recovery still under negotiation, and it declined to revise FY27 segment growth rates for now. It was evasive on inorganic deals and on EV domestic and wallet-share detail.

Powder metallurgy capacity expansion for passenger car, shock absorber and consumer durable customers

growth.why: Management guides to a sustained ~20% revenue growth run rate through festive/Q2-Q3, backed by M&HCV and PV industry growth matched by SFL, Class 8 truck orders 20-25% higher with backlogs at a 38-month high, GM EV revenue of INR200-250 crores planned and a INR1,000 crore+ new pipeline, though no capacity-level numbers were given for the top-line run rate.
